title: 3. Articles (A, An, The) & Noun Types
group: Module 1 · The Foundational Zero-to-Hero Grammar Engine
blocks: The single highest-error area for Bangla speakers. Countable vs uncountable nouns, the three articles plus the zero article, a four-step proofreading decision process, and the fixed cases.

If you fix only one chapter in this whole book, fix this one. Articles are the single highest-error area for learners whose first language does not have them, and Bangla, Hindi, Urdu, and Nepali all lack a direct equivalent of a / an / the. This is not a minor detail. Article errors are the number one reason that otherwise strong Band 7 candidates stay stuck at Band 6.0, because the mistakes are frequent, they appear in almost every sentence, and your ear cannot catch them: your first language never trained it to.
Whether you can use a / an at all depends on this distinction, so learn it before the article rules.
Countable nouns can be counted and have a plural form: one book, two books; a student, five students. They can take a / an in the singular.
Uncountable nouns are treated as a single mass and have no plural form and no a / an: information (never informations), water, advice.

The high-frequency uncountable nouns that trip up Bangladeshi candidates, worth memorising as a fixed block: information, advice, knowledge, research, equipment, furniture, accommodation, traffic, progress, news, money, water, work, luggage, baggage, software, staff, homework, feedback, transport, machinery, vocabulary.
To count an uncountable noun, use a partitive phrase (a unit word) plus of:
a study / a piece of research
a piece of furniture / an item of furniture
3.2 The three articles and the zero article
There are three articles (a, an, the) and a fourth option, no article at all, called the zero article. Every singular countable noun needs one of these four decided on purpose.

Use a / an for one, non-specific, singular, countable thing, usually mentioned for the first time. The choice between a and an depends on sound, not spelling. Use an before a vowel sound, a before a consonant sound.
a university, a European country (these begin with a “y” consonant sound)
an hour, an honest man (silent h, so a vowel sound)
an MBA, an X-ray (letter names beginning with a vowel sound)
I saw a documentary last night. (first mention, non-specific) / She wants to become an engineer. (one, non-specific)
Use the when the noun is specific: the reader or listener knows exactly which one you mean. That happens in several ways:
It was already mentioned: I saw a documentary. The documentary was about climate change.
There is only one of it: the sun, the government, the internet, the environment.
It is made specific by the words around it: the number of cars, the graph above, the capital of Bangladesh.
With superlatives and ordinals: the highest figure, the most important factor, the first step.
The chart shows the number of visitors. (both specific) / Solar power is the cleanest option available. (superlative)
Plural countable nouns talked about in general: Books are expensive. Cars cause pollution.
Uncountable nouns talked about in general: Water is essential. Education matters. Poverty is rising.
Most proper nouns: names of most countries, cities, people, languages: Bangladesh, Dhaka, English.
Education is a basic right. (general uncountable, zero article) / Cars contribute to pollution. (general plural + general uncountable)
3.3 The decision process (use this when you proofread)
When you check any singular noun, run these questions in order:
Is it countable? If no (uncountable), you cannot use a / an. Choose the (if specific) or zero article (if general). Stop.
If yes (countable): is it specific, known, or unique? If yes, use the.
If it is not specific and singular: use a / an (by sound).
If it is a general plural: use the zero article.
Some article choices are just fixed and should be learned as items:
the internet, the environment, the economy, the government, the media, the public, the world take the (treated as unique).
Superlatives always take the: the best, the largest, the most significant.
Institutions used for their purpose take zero article: go to school, go to university, go to hospital (British usage), in prison, at home. Add the only when you mean the specific building.
Countries: most take zero article (Bangladesh, France, China), but a few plural or “united/republic” names take the: the United States, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, the Philippines.
First mention then second mention: introduce with a, refer back with the. This is the classic a to the move examiners look for: The chart shows a sharp rise in 2018. The rise continued into 2019.
Because Bangla has no articles at all, the category does not exist in your mental grammar, so it must be learned as an English-only system rather than translated. Three error patterns dominate.

Error type 1 · Omitting “the” for specific and unique things.
✗ Internet has changed our lives. / Government should fund school.
✓ The internet has changed our lives. / The government should fund schools.

Error type 2 · Using “a / an” with uncountable nouns. This is the “an advice / an information” error.
✗ He gave me an advice. / She did a research on it.
✓ He gave me some advice / a piece of advice. / She did research / a study on it.

Error type 3 · Dropping the article entirely before a singular countable noun.
✗ Government should take step to reduce pollution.
✓ The government should take steps to reduce pollution.

Article control is audited densely across every task. In Task 1 a single sentence can require three separate article decisions: “The chart shows the number of visitors to a museum.” In Task 2 generalisations, the pattern flips to zero article and the: “Governments should protect the environment.” Because the errors are so frequent, they are the classic thing separating a script that reads like Band 7 in ideas but scores Band 6 in Grammatical Range and Accuracy.

Skills: Writing, Speaking
Task 1: The graph illustrates the proportion of households with an internet connection.
Task 2: Education is widely seen as the key to development, and governments should therefore fund schools properly.
Speaking Part 2: The person who influenced me most was a teacher at my primary school.
End of Chapter 3. Chapter 4 (Prepositions & Dependency Rules) follows.

title: 3. Practice · Articles (A, An, The) & Noun Types
group: Module 1 · The Foundational Zero-to-Hero Grammar Engine
blocks: Every singular countable noun needs a deliberate choice: a/an, the, or no article at all. The rule turns on one question -- is this noun specific to both writer and reader, or not?
**Why it matters:** Article errors are some of the most frequent -- and most visible -- mistakes in Bangladeshi candidates' writing, because Bangla has no article system at all.
**a/an** -- one, non-specific, singular, countable thing, usually the first mention. Choice depends on **sound, not spelling**: a university (consonant sound), an hour (silent h, vowel sound).
**the** -- the noun is specific: already mentioned, unique (the sun, the government), or made specific by the words around it (the number of cars).
**zero article** -- plurals and uncountables used in a general sense, and most proper nouns.
Ask: has this been mentioned before, or is there only one of it? If yes, use the. If it's one, unspecified example, use a/an. If neither applies, use no article at all.

blocks.title: Exercise 3.1 · Article Insertion
blocks.instructions: The articles have been removed. Rewrite each sentence inserting a, an, or the where needed. Some blanks need the zero article (no word).

items.prompt: ___ education is ___ key to ___ economic development.
items.answer: Education is the key to economic development.
accepted: Education is the key to economic development.
items.reason: General uncountable “education” and “development” take zero article; “the key” is specific.

items.prompt: She is ___ most hard-working student in ___ class.
items.answer: She is the most hard-working student in the class.
accepted: She is the most hard-working student in the class.
items.reason: Superlative and a specific class both take “the.”

items.prompt: ___ chart shows ___ number of tourists visiting ___ museum.
items.answer: The chart shows the number of tourists visiting a museum.
accepted: The chart shows the number of tourists visiting a museum.
items.reason: “the chart,” “the number of,” first-mention “a museum.”

items.prompt: ___ internet has transformed ___ way people communicate.
items.answer: The internet has transformed the way people communicate.
accepted: The internet has transformed the way people communicate.
items.reason: “the internet” is unique; “the way” is specified by the clause after it.

items.prompt: He wants to become ___ honest lawyer after ___ university.
items.answer: He wants to become an honest lawyer after university.
accepted: He wants to become an honest lawyer after university.
items.reason: “an” before the vowel sound of “honest” (silent h); “university” as an institution takes zero article.

items.prompt: ___ pollution is ___ serious problem in ___ major cities.
items.answer: Pollution is a serious problem in major cities.
accepted: Pollution is a serious problem in major cities.
items.reason: General uncountable “pollution”; “a problem” first mention; general plural “cities.”

items.prompt: I read ___ interesting article yesterday. ___ article was about ___ climate change.
items.answer: I read an interesting article yesterday. The article was about climate change.
accepted: I read an interesting article yesterday. The article was about climate change.
items.reason: First mention “an,” second mention “the,” general “climate change.”

items.prompt: ___ government should invest more in ___ public transport.
items.answer: The government should invest more in public transport.
accepted: The government should invest more in public transport.
items.reason: “the government” is specific; “public transport” is a general uncountable.

items.prompt: ___ United States and ___ United Kingdom signed ___ agreement.
items.answer: The United States and the United Kingdom signed an agreement.
accepted: The United States and the United Kingdom signed an agreement.
items.reason: These country names take “the”; “an agreement” first mention.

items.prompt: ___ sun rises in ___ east.
items.answer: The sun rises in the east.
accepted: The sun rises in the east.
items.reason: Both unique.

items.prompt: ___ poverty remains ___ obstacle to ___ progress in ___ developing world.
items.answer: Poverty remains an obstacle to progress in the developing world.
accepted: Poverty remains an obstacle to progress in the developing world.
items.reason: General “poverty” and “progress”; “an obstacle” first mention; “the developing world” is specific.

items.prompt: She gave me ___ useful advice about ___ visa process.
items.answer: She gave me useful advice about the visa process.
accepted: She gave me useful advice about the visa process.
items.reason: “advice” is uncountable (no “a”); “the visa process” is specific.

items.prompt: ___ number of ___ students who fail ___ exam is rising.
items.answer: The number of students who fail the exam is rising.
accepted: The number of students who fail the exam is rising.
items.reason: “the number of,” general “students,” the specific “exam.”

items.prompt: My brother is ___ engineer, and he works for ___ large company.
items.answer: My brother is an engineer, and he works for a large company.
accepted: My brother is an engineer, and he works for a large company.
items.reason: “an engineer” (vowel sound), “a company” first mention.

items.prompt: ___ water is essential for ___ life on ___ Earth.
items.answer: Water is essential for life on Earth.
accepted: Water is essential for life on Earth.
items.reason: General uncountables and the proper noun “Earth” take zero article.

items.prompt: We stayed in ___ hotel near ___ airport; ___ hotel was cheap.
items.answer: We stayed in a hotel near the airport; the hotel was cheap.
accepted: We stayed in a hotel near the airport; the hotel was cheap.
items.reason: First mention “a hotel,” the known “the airport,” second mention “the hotel.”

items.prompt: ___ research shows that ___ exercise improves ___ mental health.
items.answer: Research shows that exercise improves mental health.
accepted: Research shows that exercise improves mental health.
items.reason: All general/uncountable, zero article.

items.prompt: ___ environment must be protected for ___ future generations.
items.answer: The environment must be protected for future generations.
accepted: The environment must be protected for future generations.
items.reason: “the environment” is unique; “future generations” general plural.

items.prompt: He spent ___ hour reading ___ book about ___ history of ___ Bangladesh.
items.answer: He spent an hour reading a book about the history of Bangladesh.
accepted: He spent an hour reading a book about the history of Bangladesh.
items.reason: “an hour” (silent h), “a book” first mention, “the history of X” specific, proper noun “Bangladesh” zero.

items.prompt: ___ traffic in ___ capital is ___ major source of ___ air pollution.
items.answer: The traffic in the capital is a major source of air pollution.
accepted: The traffic in the capital is a major source of air pollution.
items.reason: “the traffic” specific, “the capital” specific, “a source” first mention, general “air pollution.”

items.prompt: ___ knowledge is power, but ___ information alone is not ___ knowledge.
items.answer: Knowledge is power, but information alone is not knowledge.
accepted: Knowledge is power, but information alone is not knowledge.
items.reason: All general uncountables.

items.prompt: She is ___ best doctor in ___ hospital where I work.
items.answer: She is the best doctor in the hospital where I work.
accepted: She is the best doctor in the hospital where I work.
items.reason: Superlative and a specified hospital.

items.prompt: ___ children in ___ rural areas often lack access to ___ good schools.
items.answer: Children in rural areas often lack access to good schools.
accepted: Children in rural areas often lack access to good schools.
items.reason: General plurals throughout.

items.prompt: ___ economy grew by ___ five per cent in ___ first quarter.
items.answer: The economy grew by five per cent in the first quarter.
accepted: The economy grew by five per cent in the first quarter.
items.reason: “the economy” unique, “five per cent” no article, “the first quarter” ordinal.

items.prompt: ___ solar power is ___ cleaner alternative to ___ fossil fuels.
items.answer: Solar power is a cleaner alternative to fossil fuels.
accepted: Solar power is a cleaner alternative to fossil fuels.
items.reason: General uncountable “solar power,” “a cleaner alternative” first mention, general plural “fossil fuels.”

blocks: Whether a/an is even an option depends on one distinction first: can this noun be counted? Uncountable nouns like information and advice never take a plural -s and never take a/an on their own.
**Why it matters:** This distinction decides whether article and plural rules even apply, so it has to come before everything else in Chapter 3.
**Countable nouns** can be counted and have a plural form: one book, two books. They take a/an in the singular.
**Uncountable nouns** are a single mass, with **no plural form** and **no a/an**: information (never informations), water, advice.
The high-frequency IELTS set to memorise
information, advice, knowledge, research, equipment, furniture, accommodation, traffic, progress, news, money, work, luggage, software, staff, homework.
Use a **partitive phrase**: not an advice but a piece of advice; not a furniture but a piece of furniture or an item of furniture.

blocks.title: Exercise 3.2 · Countable versus Uncountable Error Spotting
blocks.instructions: Each sentence misuses a noun, usually by giving an uncountable noun a plural -s or an a / an. Rewrite each sentence correctly.

items.prompt: The teacher gave us many useful advices before the exam.
items.answer: The teacher gave us much useful advice before the exam.
accepted: The teacher gave us much useful advice before the exam.
items.reason: “advice” is uncountable: no plural, use “much” not “many.”

items.prompt: I need some informations about the application process.
items.answer: I need some information about the application process.
accepted: I need some information about the application process.
items.reason: “information” is uncountable.

items.prompt: She bought new furnitures for her apartment.
items.answer: She bought new furniture for her apartment.
accepted: She bought new furniture for her apartment.
items.reason: “furniture” has no plural; use “pieces of furniture” if counting.

items.prompt: The laboratory does not have enough equipments.
items.answer: The laboratory does not have enough equipment.
accepted: The laboratory does not have enough equipment.
items.reason: “equipment” is uncountable.

items.prompt: He has made a good progress in his studies this year.
items.answer: He has made good progress in his studies this year.
accepted: He has made good progress in his studies this year.
items.reason: “progress” is uncountable: no “a.”

items.prompt: The researchers published several important researches last year.
items.answer: The researchers published several important studies last year.
accepted: The researchers published several important studies last year.
items.reason: “research” is uncountable; the countable word is “studies.”

items.prompt: We had a lot of homeworks during the holidays.
items.answer: We had a lot of homework during the holidays.
accepted: We had a lot of homework during the holidays.
items.reason: “homework” is uncountable.

items.prompt: The company installed new softwares on every computer.
items.answer: The company installed new software on every computer.
accepted: The company installed new software on every computer.
items.reason: “software” is uncountable.

items.prompt: There were many traffics on the road this morning.
items.answer: There was heavy traffic on the road this morning.
accepted: There was heavy traffic on the road this morning.
items.reason: “traffic” is uncountable: no plural, and “was,” not “were.”

items.prompt: The hotel provides free accommodations for its staffs.
items.answer: The hotel provides free accommodation for its staff.
accepted: The hotel provides free accommodation for its staff.
items.reason: both uncountable: no plural.

items.prompt: My knowledges of physics are quite limited.
items.answer: My knowledge of physics is quite limited.
accepted: My knowledge of physics is quite limited.
items.reason: “knowledge” is uncountable and singular.

items.prompt: The government spent a huge money on the project.
items.answer: The government spent a huge amount of money on the project.
accepted: The government spent a huge amount of money on the project.
items.reason: “money” is uncountable: no “a” directly.

items.prompt: She gave me two good news yesterday.
items.answer: She gave me some good news yesterday.
accepted: She gave me some good news yesterday.
She gave me two pieces of good news yesterday.
items.reason: “news” is uncountable despite the final -s.

items.prompt: The students carried heavy luggages to the airport.
items.answer: The students carried heavy luggage to the airport.
accepted: The students carried heavy luggage to the airport.
items.reason: “luggage” is uncountable; count with “pieces of luggage.”

items.prompt: The report contains many useful datas about the economy.
items.answer: The report contains much useful data about the economy.
accepted: The report contains much useful data about the economy.
items.reason: “data” is treated as uncountable/mass here; “datas” is never correct.
